narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Tells the prose frame and introduces each speech.

job.name: Job
job.note: Upright man of Hus, father of ten grown children, stricken and lamenting.

2.t: O that my sins, whereby I have deserved wrath, and the calamity that I suffer, were weighed in a balance.

3.t: As the sand of the sea, this would appear heavier: therefore, my words are full of sorrow:

4.t: For the arrows of the Lord are in me, the rage whereof drinketh up my spirit, and the terrors of the Lord war against me.

5.t: Will the wild ass bray when he hath grass? or will the ox low when he standeth before a full manger?

6.t: Or can an unsavoury thing be eaten, that is not seasoned with salt? or can a man taste that which, when tasted, bringeth death?

7.t: The things which before my soul would not touch, now, through anguish, are my meats.

8.t: Who will grant that my request may come: and that God may give me what I look for?

9.t: And that he that hath begun may destroy me, that he may let loose his hand, and cut me off?

10.t: And that this may be my comfort, that afflicting me with sorrow, he spare not, nor I contradict the words of the Holy one.

11.t: For what is my strength, that I can hold out? or what is my end, that I should keep patience?

12.t: My strength is not the strength of stones, nor is my flesh of brass.

13.t: Behold there is no help for me in myself, and my familiar friends also are departed from me.

14.t: He that taketh away mercy from his friend, forsaketh the fear of the Lord.

15.t: My brethren have passed by me, as the torrent that passeth swiftly in the valleys.

16.t: They that fear the hoary frost, the snow shall fall upon them.

17.t: At the time when they shall be scattered they shall perish: and after it groweth hot, they shall be melted out of their place.

18.t: The paths of their steps are entangled: they shall walk in vain, and shall perish.

19.t: Consider the paths of Thema, the ways of Saba, and wait a little while.

20.t: They are confounded, because I have hoped: they are come also even unto me, and are covered with shame.

21.t: Now you are come: and now, seeing my affliction, you are afraid.

22.t: Did I say: Bring to me, and give me of your substance?

23.t: Or deliver me from the hand of the enemy, and rescue me out of the hand of the mighty?

24.t: Teach me, and I will hold my peace: and if I have been ignorant of any thing, instruct me.

25.t: Why have you detracted the words of truth, whereas there is none of you that can reprove me?

26.t: You dress up speeches only to rebuke, and you utter words to the wind.

27.t: You rush in upon the fatherless, and you endeavour to overthrow your friend.

28.t: However, finish what you have begun: give ear and see whether I lie.

29.t: Answer, I beseech you, without contention: and speaking that which is just, judge ye.

30.t: And you shall not find iniquity in my tongue, neither shall folly sound in my mouth.
